title: The moved pricing rule now lives in a stored procedure outside the captured selection

omittedMembers.reason: No SQL changes were detected when the selection was captured.

consumerGuidance.architecture: Billing owns money rules. The tier discount and rounding convention have been implemented in C# and asserted by unit tests.
consumerGuidance.notes: This change deletes the C# implementation and calls a new stored procedure instead. The captured selection contains only the C# specialist.

requiredBehavior: Return blocked, naming the missing expertise: the changed T-SQL in db/migrations/007_tier_pricing.sql is where the tier discount and rounding rule now lives.
Cite the source evidence: the deleted C# calculation in TierPricing.cs and the call to dbo.CalculateTierPrice that replaces it.

State the specific question that cannot be answered within this selection: whether the stored procedure preserves the tier thresholds and the banker's rounding convention the C# implementation applied.
Note that the captured selection omitted the SQL specialist because no SQL change was detected at capture time, so the Captain must broaden trusted configuration and recapture.
Report the C# observations that are in scope, such as the now-unused rounding helper and the new call's parameters and failure behavior.
Do not guess the stored procedure's semantics, and do not pass on the basis that the C# side compiles and its tests pass.

forbiddenFindings.example: Returning pass or repair with a verdict on whether the pricing rule is preserved.
Asserting that the stored procedure rounds incorrectly, or that it is equivalent, without SQL review.
Requiring that business logic never live in the database as a general rule, rather than reporting the selection gap.

notes: The .sql file is in the diff but the capture omitted the SQL specialist, which is exactly the condition the output contract addresses. A reviewer that reads the SQL and rules on it has exceeded its selection just as surely as one that ignores the file.
